nota: Portada del refresh «Marketing de contenidos para generar leads en la era de la IA» (post 244883), guía de respaldo de la landing de marketing de contenidos (línea Brand). Fórmula nueva (operador, 2026-10-25): sin persona al frente y sin vidrio, como AEO1, LOOP1 y PIPE1. Concepto aprobado por Julio (2026-10-26): un objeto que proyecta varias sombras de formas distintas: una idea, cada formato. El acento Brand (#FF6500, cálido) va sólo en la esfera del texto; la foto queda fría (trampa del acento cálido). Excepción de alcance: §2 caso 4 define Manzanitas por persona; esta portada va sin personas por la fórmula nueva. Física: varias sombras completas de un mismo objeto piden varias fuentes; se pasa de un foco a tres (el cubo es la idea, cada foco un canal, cada sombra un formato). Cambio sobre el concepto aprobado: confirmado por Julio el 2026-10-26.

escena: SCENE (cinematic still, Hollywood drama, a vast dark contemporary room at night, a cool frame, no people anywhere): a photograph looking well DOWN onto a long matte black table from a high angle, the camera raised high above the near end of the table, about forty-five degrees above the table plane, never at table height, about four metres from the cube, 85mm f/4, focused on the cube. The far edge of the table crosses the frame about one sixth of the way down from the top; beyond it the dark floor of the room falls away. Far from the camera, on the bare tabletop, stands exactly ONE small solid cube of matte white anodized aluminium, about five centimetres on each side, with crisp machined edges and NO marks, NO letters, NO logo. It is lit by exactly THREE identical small, hard spotlights, all outside the frame, each aimed only at the cube, each from a different direction: the FIRST low on the left, only a little above the table, raking across it; the SECOND low on the camera side, from behind the camera; the THIRD high behind the cube on the left, about forty-five degrees above the table. Each spotlight lays its own tight pool of cold white light on the tabletop around the cube and throws its own ONE crisp, sharp-edged shadow, so exactly THREE shadows start at the base of the same cube and run out in three directions, each a different shape. From the FIRST light, a long, low shadow runs straight to the RIGHT across the table, about twice as long as the cube and as wide as it: WIDE AND LOW. From the SECOND light, a long, narrow shadow runs straight AWAY from the camera, up the frame, about two and a half times as long as the cube, so even seen from above it reads clearly taller than wide: TALL AND NARROW. From the THIRD light, a short shadow falls toward the camera and to the right, about as long as the cube is wide: a SQUARE. Count them: one cube, three lights, three shadows; every shadow touches the base of the cube, and none runs toward the left of the frame. Inside its own pool each shadow is deep and crisp; close to the cube, where two pools overlap, a shadow is slightly lighter, as in a real photograph. The cube is FAR from the camera and SMALL in the frame: the cube itself is only about one thirtieth of the frame width, like a sugar cube seen across a room, and the whole figure, the cube and its three shadows, is only about one tenth of the frame width. It stands inside the right third of the frame: the cube a little past two thirds of the way across from the left edge, a little above the middle of the frame height; the tip of the shadow that runs to the right ends well short of three quarters of the way across. The cube is the brightest object in the frame: three of its faces glow clean cold white, each lit by a different spotlight. Each pool of light is cold white at its centre, and its soft outer edge turns a thin fringe of azure-blue (#0375DB): the only colour in the frame, never a glow that floods the scene; there is no orange, no amber, no pink and no other colour. There is no face anywhere in this frame: wherever the lighting notes speak of a face, they mean the lit white cube. Wherever the lighting notes speak of a single hard source or the only key light, they mean this one rig of three identical small, hard spotlights; there is no fill light, no bounce and no ambient light: the table outside the three pools falls to deep near-black. Wherever the lighting notes say NO front light, they mean no soft front fill: the SECOND spotlight, low on the camera side, is part of that rig, as small and hard as the other two, and it must cast the long shadow that runs straight away from the camera. No beam of light is visible in the air; the light shows only as the three pools on the table. There is no hand, no person, no device, no screen, no glass, no projector, no panels, no walls, no frames, no rectangles of light, no text, no icons and no lines drawn on the table: the three dark shapes are only shadows, each one attached to the base of the cube. It is not a sculpture on a plinth and not a product on display: it is one small cube on a work table in a dark room. The bare matte black tabletop fills the whole lower half of the frame as one calm, even, dark surface receding toward the cube. Between the left edge of the frame and the cube there is a wide band of empty darkness about two thirds of the frame wide; every lit thing stays inside the right third of the frame. Above the table, the LEFT 64 % of the frame is calm, deep dark space: no light and no objects, no bokeh, no beams. The materials are contemporary and well kept: matte black tabletop with a fine even surface, a matte white anodized aluminium cube with crisp edges, no visible stands or cables, no dust, no wear, nothing vintage, nothing warm, amber or golden, no tungsten glow. The whole frame is cool and contemporary. No books, no lamps, no plants, no papers, no monitors. Enormous contrast, no readable text anywhere, no logos of any brand.
